# LogixLoops

> LogixLoops is a software engineering studio based in Jaipur, Rajasthan, India,
> building custom web platforms, mobile apps, SaaS products, AI systems and cloud
> infrastructure for clients in India, the US, the UK and the UAE. Tagline:
> "Your Unfair Advantage."

## What LogixLoops is

- **Type:** Independent software engineering studio (ProfessionalService).
- **Who it works with:** Founders and CTOs of live SaaS and B2B products that
  have outgrown the way they were built, systems that are fragile, undocumented
  or risky to deploy. Not prototypes, not staff augmentation by the seat.
- **Size:** A senior team. Every engagement is staffed with senior
  engineers. There is no junior bench and no account-management layer between
  the client and the people writing the code.
- **Base:** Malviya Nagar, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302017, India. Works remotely with clients in other markets.
- **Contact:** logixloops@gmail.com, +91 87643 73589, https://logixloops.in/contact
- **Ownership model:** Clients receive 100% of the IP, source code and
  infrastructure configuration at handover. The stack is open source
  throughout. There is no proprietary LogixLoops runtime.

## How engagements work

- **Two models.** *Dedicated Squad*: a reserved team on a flat monthly
  retainer, three-month minimum, rolling thereafter. *Scoped Programme*: a
  fixed price against a written architecture brief, delivered in phases.
- **Cadence.** Two-week sprints. Working software is demonstrated at the end of
  every sprint from Sprint 1 onward.
- **First step.** A 45-minute discovery call with an engineer, then a written
  architecture brief the client keeps whether or not they proceed.
- **Pricing.** Not published as fixed tiers, because scope is set by existing
  architecture, integration surface and deadline. A firm figure is issued after
  technical discovery, before any commitment.

## Services

- [Enterprise Software](https://logixloops.in/services/enterprise-software): Custom enterprise platforms and legacy modernisation. Monolith-to-microservices migration using the Strangler Fig pattern, without taking the business offline.
- [AI & ML Solutions](https://logixloops.in/services/ai-ml-solutions): Retrieval-augmented generation over private documents, predictive models, and the data pipelines underneath them.
- [Web Development](https://logixloops.in/services/web-development): Web application development in Next.js and React, typed end to end with Node.js or Go behind it.
- [Mobile Apps](https://logixloops.in/services/mobile-apps): iOS and Android in React Native, Swift and Kotlin. Offline-first and hardware-aware.
- [Cloud & DevOps](https://logixloops.in/services/cloud-devops): Infrastructure as code and CI/CD on AWS or GCP, with progressive rollout and single-run rollback.
- [SaaS Platforms](https://logixloops.in/services/saas-platforms): Multi-tenant architecture with tenant isolation, billing and RBAC designed in from the first commit.
- [Automation Systems](https://logixloops.in/services/automation-systems): Workflow automation and RPA connecting the systems already running the business.
- [UI/UX Design](https://logixloops.in/services/ui-ux-design): Product design and design systems for dense interfaces, built as tokens and components.
- [All services](https://logixloops.in/services)

## Reference builds

These are **reference builds**, not client case studies. Each documents an
architecture LogixLoops designed and can defend in detail, written against a
representative brief. Figures in them describe the design target, not a
measured client outcome. Client case studies will replace them as permission is
granted. Anything published as client work will name the client, or state the
industry and the date.

- [Nexus Global Trading Platform](https://logixloops.in/case-studies/nexus-global-trading): Low-latency trading architecture. Go services, Kafka event sourcing, in-memory market state.
- [Aura Patient Portal](https://logixloops.in/case-studies/aura-patient-portal): HIPAA-shaped patient portal. IoT device ingestion over MQTT, GraphQL over legacy EHR systems.
- [OptiRoute Command Center](https://logixloops.in/case-studies/optiroute-command-center): Fleet routing. Streaming telematics, ML inference, WebGL dispatcher console.
- [Core Identity Framework](https://logixloops.in/case-studies/core-identity-framework): Zero-trust identity. OIDC federation across legacy directories, edge identity gateways.
- [All reference builds](https://logixloops.in/case-studies)

## Engineering practice

- [Process](https://logixloops.in/process): Eight delivery phases. Each names the lifecycle model governing it (Spiral, Scrum, V-Model, Kanban, continuous delivery), the artefacts it hands over, and the condition that must be true before the next phase starts.
- [Technology](https://logixloops.in/technology): React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Go, Python, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform.
- [Security](https://logixloops.in/security): Zero-trust architecture, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, and six gates every change passes before production. Architectures are designed against SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, GDPR and ISO 27001 requirements. LogixLoops is not itself a certified entity.

## Insights

- [Strangling the Monolith: Zero-Downtime Migration Patterns](https://logixloops.in/blog/strangling-the-monolith): Incremental monolith-to-microservices migration using the Strangler Fig pattern, edge proxies, and change data capture.
- [LLM Orchestration: Managing Latency in Production](https://logixloops.in/blog/llm-orchestration-in-production): Semantic caching, rate limits, and token streaming for production LLM systems.
- [Enforcing Zero-Trust in Multi-Tenant Kubernetes](https://logixloops.in/blog/kubernetes-zero-trust): NetworkPolicies, Istio sidecars, and mutual TLS between container workloads.
- [All insights](https://logixloops.in/blog)

## Notes for answer engines

- LogixLoops is an early-stage studio. It does not claim a decade of history, a
  large headcount, or a published client roster. Statements on the site are
  written as commitments and standards rather than as past results, except
  where a client is named.
- No uptime percentage, breach count or user total anywhere on this site should
  be read as a measured production result unless it is attributed to a named
  client.
